Class UserAccount

java.lang.Object
app.user.UserAccount
@Entity public class UserAccount extends Object
A read-only view of the credential record the auth service owns.

Authentication state lives in user_accounts, written only by the NestJS auth service. This service reads it because two of its values must be current at the moment they are used rather than as of whenever the caller's token was signed:

  • accountStatus gates order placement. A token stays valid for fifteen minutes, so a deactivated trader would keep trading for that long if the check read a claim instead of this table.
  • userRole is reported on the caller's profile, where it should reflect the account as it stands.

Marked Immutable so Hibernate silently discards any attempt to update it: the auth service is the only writer, and that is enforced here rather than left to convention.

password_hash, failed_login_attempts and locked_until are deliberately not mapped. This service has no use for them, and an unmapped column cannot be read by accident or logged.

    • UserAccount

      public UserAccount(UUID userId, String email, String userRole, String accountStatus)
      Creates a record directly, for tests that stand in for the auth service.

      There is no repository method that writes this table, so constructing one here cannot persist it through this service.

      Parameters:
      userId - the account id
      email - the login email
      userRole - ADMIN or TRADER
      accountStatus - ACTIVE or DEACTIVATED
